questions.text: Let $z$ be the complex number satisfying $|z-5|\le3$ and having maximum positive principal argument. Then $34\left|\dfrac{5z-12}{5iz+16}\right|^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
The region is the disc with centre 5 and radius 3. The argument is largest at the point where the tangent from O touches the circle: $|z|=\sqrt{25-9}=4$ and $\sin\theta=\dfrac35$.
So $z=4\left(\dfrac45+\dfrac35i\right)=\dfrac{16+12i}{5}$.
$5z-12=4+12i$ and $5iz+16=(-12+16i)+16=4+16i$.
$34\cdot\dfrac{16+144}{16+256}=34\cdot\dfrac{160}{272}=20$.

questions.text: The positive integer n, for which the solutions of the equation $x(x+2)+(x+2)(x+4)+\cdots+(x+2n-2)(x+2n)=\dfrac{8n}{3}$ are two consecutive even integers, is :
questions.sol:
LHS $=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(x+2k)(x+2k+2)=nx^2+2n^2x+\dfrac{4(n-1)n(n+1)}{3}$.
Dividing by $n$: $x^2+2nx+\dfrac{4n^2-12}{3}=0$.
Roots differ by 2, so the discriminant is 4: $4n^2-\dfrac{4(4n^2-12)}{3}=4 \Rightarrow n^2=9$, $n=3$.
Check: $x^2+6x+8=0$ gives $-2,-4$, consecutive even integers.

questions.text: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^2+2ax+(3a+10)=0$ such that $\alpha<1<\beta$. Then the set of all possible values of a is :
questions.sol:
For an upward parabola, 1 lies strictly between the roots exactly when $f(1)<0$.
$f(1)=1+2a+3a+10=5a+11<0 \Rightarrow a<-\dfrac{11}{5}$.
(Then the roots are automatically real and distinct.)

questions.text: For the matrices $A=\begin{bmatrix}3&-4\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}-29&49\\-13&18\end{bmatrix}$, if $\left(A^{15}+B\right)\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\0\end{bmatrix}$, then among the following which one is true ?
questions.sol:
Write $A=I+N$ with $N=\begin{bmatrix}2&-4\\1&-2\end{bmatrix}$; $N^2=O$.
So $A^{15}=I+15N=\begin{bmatrix}31&-60\\15&-29\end{bmatrix}$ and $A^{15}+B=\begin{bmatrix}2&-11\\2&-11\end{bmatrix}$.
The system reduces to $2x=11y$; among the options only $x=11, y=2$ satisfies it.

questions.text:
If the system of equations
$3x+y+4z=3$
$2x+\alpha y-z=-3$
$x+2y+z=4$
has no solution, then the value of $\alpha$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}3&1&4\\2&\alpha&-1\\1&2&1\end{vmatrix}=3(\alpha+2)-1(2+1)+4(4-\alpha)=19-\alpha$.
No solution needs $\Delta=0$, so $\alpha=19$.
Then $\Delta_x=\begin{vmatrix}3&1&4\\-3&19&-1\\4&2&1\end{vmatrix}=3(21)-1(1)+4(-82)=-266\neq0$, so the system is indeed inconsistent.

questions.text: Let $a_1, \dfrac{a_2}{2}, \dfrac{a_3}{2^2}, \ldots, \dfrac{a_{10}}{2^9}$ be a G.P. of common ratio $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$. If $a_1+a_2+\ldots+a_{10}=62$, then $a_1$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{a_k}{2^{k-1}}=a_1\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)^{k-1} \Rightarrow a_k=a_1(\sqrt2)^{k-1}$.
$\sum_{k=1}^{10}a_k=a_1\dfrac{(\sqrt2)^{10}-1}{\sqrt2-1}=\dfrac{31a_1}{\sqrt2-1}=62$.
$a_1=2(\sqrt2-1)$.

questions.text: A random variable X takes values 0, 1, 2, 3 with probabilities $\dfrac{2a+1}{30}, \dfrac{8a-1}{30}, \dfrac{4a+1}{30}$, b respectively, where $a, b\in\mathbf{R}$. Let $\mu$ and $\sigma$ respectively be the mean and standard deviation of X such that $\sigma^2+\mu^2=2$. Then $\dfrac{a}{b}$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Total probability: $\dfrac{14a+1}{30}+b=1$.
$\sigma^2+\mu^2=E(X^2)=\dfrac{8a-1}{30}+\dfrac{4(4a+1)}{30}+9b=\dfrac{24a+3}{30}+9b=2$.
Substituting $b=\dfrac{29-14a}{30}$: $24a+3+261-126a=60 \Rightarrow a=2$, $b=\dfrac1{30}$.
$\dfrac ab=60$.

questions.text: Let one end of a focal chord of the parabola $y^2=16x$ be $(16, 16)$. If $P(\alpha, \beta)$ divides this focal chord internally in the ratio $5:2$, then the minimum value of $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
With $a=4$, $(16,16)=(4t^2,8t)$ gives $t=2$; the other end has $t^\prime=-\dfrac1t=-\dfrac12$, i.e. $(1,-4)$.
Dividing in $5:2$ from $(16,16)$: $\left(\dfrac{5+32}{7},\dfrac{-20+32}{7}\right)=\left(\dfrac{37}{7},\dfrac{12}{7}\right)$, sum $7$.
From the other end: $\left(\dfrac{82}{7},\dfrac{72}{7}\right)$, sum $22$.
Minimum $=7$.

questions.text: Let $y^2=12x$ be the parabola with its vertex at O. Let P be a point on the parabola and A be a point on the $x$-axis such that $\angle OPA=90^\circ$. Then the locus of the centroid of such triangles OPA is :
questions.sol:
P$=(3t^2,6t)$, A$=(h,0)$. Slopes: OP $=\dfrac2t$, PA $=\dfrac{6t}{3t^2-h}$.
Perpendicular: $\dfrac{12}{3t^2-h}=-1 \Rightarrow h=3t^2+12$.
Centroid: $X=\dfrac{6t^2+12}{3}=2t^2+4$, $Y=2t$, so $X=\dfrac{Y^2}{2}+4$.
Locus: $y^2-2x+8=0$.

questions.text: If the line $\alpha x+4y=\sqrt{7}$, where $\alpha\in\mathbf{R}$, touches the ellipse $3x^2+4y^2=1$ at the point P in the first quadrant, then one of the focal distances of P is :
questions.sol:
Ellipse: $a^2=\dfrac13$, $b^2=\dfrac14$, $e^2=1-\dfrac34=\dfrac14$.
The tangent at $(x_1,y_1)$ is $3x_1x+4y_1y=1$; comparing with $\dfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt7}x+\dfrac{4}{\sqrt7}y=1$ gives $y_1=\dfrac1{\sqrt7}$, and then $3x_1^2=1-\dfrac47$, $x_1=\dfrac1{\sqrt7}$ (first quadrant).
Focal distances $a\pm ex_1=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\pm\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt7}$.

questions.text: For a triangle ABC, let $\vec{p}=\overrightarrow{BC}$, $\vec{q}=\overrightarrow{CA}$ and $\vec{r}=\overrightarrow{BA}$. If $|\vec{p}|=2\sqrt{3}$, $|\vec{q}|=2$ and $\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\vec{p}$ and $\vec{q}$, then $\left|\vec{p}\times\left(\vec{q}-3\vec{r}\right)\right|^2+3|\vec{r}|^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\vec r=\overrightarrow{BA}=\overrightarrow{BC}+\overrightarrow{CA}=\vec p+\vec q$, so $\vec q-3\vec r=-3\vec p-2\vec q$ and $\vec p\times(\vec q-3\vec r)=-2\,\vec p\times\vec q$.
$|\vec p\times\vec q|^2=12\cdot4\cdot\left(1-\dfrac13\right)=32$, so the first term is $4\times32=128$.
$\vec p\cdot\vec q=2\sqrt3\cdot2\cdot\dfrac1{\sqrt3}=4$, $|\vec r|^2=12+4+8=24$, so $3|\vec r|^2=72$.
Total $=200$.

questions.text:
Let $f:\mathbf{R}\to\mathbf{R}$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f''(x)>0$ for all $x\in\mathbf{R}$ and $f'(a-1)=0$, where a is a real number. Let $g(x)=f(\tan^2x-2\tan x+a)$, $0<x<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
Consider the following two statements :
(I) g is increasing in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$
(II) g is deceasing in $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$
Then,
questions.sol:
Let $u=\tan^2x-2\tan x+a=(\tan x-1)^2+a-1\ge a-1$. Since $f'$ is increasing and $f'(a-1)=0$, $f'(u)\ge0$ (zero only at $x=\dfrac\pi4$).
$g'(x)=f'(u)\cdot2(\tan x-1)\sec^2x$: negative on $\left(0,\dfrac\pi4\right)$, positive on $\left(\dfrac\pi4,\dfrac\pi2\right)$.
So g decreases then increases; neither statement is true.

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\sec x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-2y=2+3\sin x$, $x\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $y(0)=-\dfrac{7}{4}$. Then $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}-2y\cos x=(2+3\sin x)\cos x$; integrating factor $e^{-2\sin x}$.
With $s=\sin x$: $ye^{-2s}=\displaystyle\int(2+3s)e^{-2s}ds=-\frac{(2+3s)}{2}e^{-2s}-\frac34e^{-2s}+C$.
So $y=-\dfrac{2+3s}{2}-\dfrac34+Ce^{2s}$; $y(0)=-\dfrac74 \Rightarrow C=0$.
$y\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)=-\dfrac{3.5}{2}-\dfrac34=-\dfrac52$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the area of the region $\{(x, y):1-2x\le y\le4-x^2, x\ge0, y\ge0\}$ is $\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}$, $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbf{N}$, $\gcd(\alpha, \beta)=1$, then the value of $(\alpha+\beta)$ is :
questions.sol:
The region lies under $y=4-x^2$ for $0\le x\le2$, above the $x$-axis, and above the line $y=1-2x$ (which matters only for $0\le x\le\dfrac12$).
Area $=\displaystyle\int_0^2(4-x^2)dx-\int_0^{1/2}(1-2x)dx=\frac{16}{3}-\frac14=\frac{61}{12}$.
$\alpha+\beta=73$.

questions.sol:
$\dfrac{1}{{}^{n}C_r}+\dfrac{1}{{}^{n}C_{r+1}}=\dfrac{r!(n-r-1)!\,[(n-r)+(r+1)]}{n!}=\dfrac{n+1}{n}\cdot\dfrac{1}{{}^{n-1}C_r}$.
With $n=15$, each factor is $\dfrac{16}{15}\cdot\dfrac{1}{{}^{14}C_r}$, for $r=0,\ldots,12$ (13 factors).
So $\alpha=\dfrac{16}{15}$ and $30\alpha=32$.

questions.text: If P is a point on the circle $x^2+y^2=4$, Q is a point on the straight line $5x+y+2=0$ and $x-y+1=0$ is the perpendicular bisector of PQ, then 13 times the sum of abscissa of all such points P is __________.
questions.sol:
Q is the mirror image of P$(a,b)$ in $x-y+1=0$: Q$=(b-1,\,a+1)$.
Q on $5x+y+2=0$: $5(b-1)+a+1+2=0 \Rightarrow a=2-5b$.
On the circle: $(2-5b)^2+b^2=4 \Rightarrow 26b^2-20b=0 \Rightarrow b=0$ or $\dfrac{10}{13}$, giving $a=2$ or $-\dfrac{24}{13}$.
$13\left(2-\dfrac{24}{13}\right)=2$.

questions.text: Let the maximum value of $(\sin^{-1}x)^2+(\cos^{-1}x)^2$ for $x\in\left[-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right]$ be $\dfrac{m}{n}\pi^2$, where $\gcd(m, n)=1$. Then $m+n$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Let $t=\sin^{-1}x\in\left[-\dfrac\pi3,\dfrac\pi4\right]$; then $\cos^{-1}x=\dfrac\pi2-t$ and the expression is $2t^2-\pi t+\dfrac{\pi^2}{4}$, an upward parabola, so the maximum is at an end point.
$t=-\dfrac\pi3$: $\dfrac{2\pi^2}{9}+\dfrac{\pi^2}{3}+\dfrac{\pi^2}{4}=\dfrac{29\pi^2}{36}$; $t=\dfrac\pi4$: $\dfrac{\pi^2}{8}$.
So $\dfrac mn=\dfrac{29}{36}$ and $m+n=65$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $[\cdot]$ denote the greatest integer function and $f(x)=\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n^3}\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left[\frac{k^2}{3^x}\right]$. Then $12\displaystyle\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}f(j)$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Let $c=3^{-x}$. Since $ck^2-1<[ck^2]\le ck^2$, the sum lies between $c\sum k^2-n$ and $c\sum k^2$; dividing by $n^3$, both bounds tend to $\dfrac c3$.
So $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{3\cdot3^x}$ and $\sum_{j\ge1}f(j)=\dfrac13\cdot\dfrac{1/3}{1-1/3}=\dfrac16$.
$12\times\dfrac16=2$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\int_0^1 4\cot^{-1}(1-2x+4x^2)\,dx=a\tan^{-1}(2)-b\log_e(5)$, where $a, b\in\mathbf{N}$, then $(2a+b)$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Put $u=2x$: integral $=2\displaystyle\int_0^2\cot^{-1}(1-u+u^2)\,du=2\int_0^2\left[\tan^{-1}u-\tan^{-1}(u-1)\right]du$.
$\displaystyle\int_0^2\tan^{-1}(u-1)\,du=\int_{-1}^{1}\tan^{-1}v\,dv=0$ (odd).
$\displaystyle\int_0^2\tan^{-1}u\,du=2\tan^{-1}2-\frac12\log_e5$, so the integral is $4\tan^{-1}2-\log_e5$.
$a=4$, $b=1$, $2a+b=9$.

questions.text: Keeping the significant figures in view, the sum of the physical quantities 52.01 m, 153.2 m and 0.123 m is :
questions.sol:
Exact sum $=205.333$ m. In addition the result keeps the fewest decimal places among the terms (one, from 153.2 m).
So the sum is 205.3 m.

questions.text: A spherical body of radius $r$ and density $\sigma$ falls freely through a viscous liquid having density $\rho$ and viscosity $\eta$ and attains a terminal velocity $v_0$. Estimated maximum error in the quantity $\eta$ is : (Ignore errors associated with $\sigma$, $\rho$ and $g$, gravitational acceleration)
questions.sol:
Terminal velocity: $v_0=\dfrac{2r^2(\sigma-\rho)g}{9\eta}$, so $\eta=\dfrac{2r^2(\sigma-\rho)g}{9v_0}\propto\dfrac{r^2}{v_0}$.
Maximum relative error: $\dfrac{\Delta\eta}{\eta}=\dfrac{2\Delta r}{r}+\dfrac{\Delta v_0}{v_0}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A river of width 200 m is flowing from west to east with a speed of 18 km/h. A boat, moving with speed of 36 km/h in still water, is made to travel one-round trip (bank to bank of the river). Minimum time taken by the boat for this journey and also the displacement along the river bank are _______ and _______ respectively.
questions.sol:
Boat speed 10 m/s, river 5 m/s. Minimum time means heading straight across: $\dfrac{200}{10}=20$ s each way, 40 s in all.
In each crossing the river carries the boat $5\times20=100$ m downstream (east), in the same direction both ways.
Total displacement along the bank $=200$ m.

questions.text: The pulley shown in figure is made using a thin rim and two rods of length equal to diameter of the rim. The rim and each rod have a mass of $M$. Two blocks of mass of $M$ and $m$ are attached to two ends of a light string passing over the pulley, which is hinged to rotate freely in vertical plane about its center. The magnitudes of the acceleration experienced by the blocks is __________ (assume no slipping of string on pulley).
questions.sol:
Moment of inertia: rim $MR^2$; each rod (length $2R$) about its centre $\dfrac{M(2R)^2}{12}=\dfrac{MR^2}{3}$. Total $I=\dfrac{5}{3}MR^2$.
$a=\dfrac{(M-m)g}{M+m+I/R^2}=\dfrac{(M-m)g}{\left(\dfrac83\right)M+m}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two cars $A$ and $B$ each of mass $10^3$ kg are moving on parallel tracks separated by a distance of 10 m, in same direction with speeds 72 km/h and 36 km/h. The magnitude of angular momentum of car $A$ with respect to car $B$ is __________ J.s.
questions.sol:
Velocity of A relative to B $=20-10=10$ m/s, along the tracks; perpendicular distance $=10$ m.
$L=mv_{rel}d=10^3\times10\times10=10^5$ J s.

questions.text: A body of mass 2 kg is moving along $x$-direction such that its displacement as function of time is given by $x(t)=\alpha t^2+\beta t+\gamma$ m, where $\alpha=1\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, $\beta=1$ m/s and $\gamma=1$ m. The work done on the body during the time interval $t=2$ s to $t=3$ s, is _________ J.
questions.sol:
$v=2\alpha t+\beta=2t+1$: $v(2)=5$ m/s, $v(3)=7$ m/s.
Work-energy theorem: $W=\dfrac12\times2\times(49-25)=24$ J.

questions.text: A large drum having radius $R$ is spinning around its axis with angular velocity $\omega$, as shown in figure. The minimum value of $\omega$ so that a body of mass $M$ remains stuck to the inner wall of the drum, taking the coefficient of friction between the drum surface and mass $M$ as $\mu$, is :
questions.sol:
The wall provides the normal reaction $N=M\omega^2R$ (centripetal force).
Friction must hold the weight: $\mu N\ge Mg \Rightarrow \mu M\omega^2R\ge Mg$.
$\omega_{min}=\sqrt{\dfrac{g}{\mu R}}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Surface tension of two liquids (having same densities), $T_1$ and $T_2$, are measured using capillary rise method utilizing two tubes with inner radii of $r_1$ and $r_2$ where $r_1>r_2$. The measured liquid heights in these tubes are $h_1$ and $h_2$ respectively. [Ignore the weight of the liquid about the lowest point of miniscus]. The heights $h_1$ and $h_2$ and surfaces tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$ satisfy the relation :
questions.sol:
Capillary rise $h=\dfrac{2T\cos\theta}{r\rho g}$, so with equal densities $\dfrac{h_1}{h_2}=\dfrac{T_1}{T_2}\cdot\dfrac{r_2}{r_1}$, where $\dfrac{r_2}{r_1}<1$.
If $T_1=T_2$ then $h_1<h_2$ (option 4 is consistent; options 1 and 3 are not). If $T_1<T_2$ then $h_1<h_2$ as well, so option 2 is impossible.
The final key takes option (4).

questions.text: The r.m.s. speed of oxygen molecules at $47^\circ$C is equal to that of the hydrogen molecules kept at __________ $^\circ$C. (Mass of oxygen molecule/mass of hydrogen molecule $=32/2$)
questions.sol:
$v_{rms}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$; equal speeds need $\dfrac{T}{M}$ equal.
$T_{H_2}=320\times\dfrac{2}{32}=20$ K $=-253^\circ$C.

questions.text: The kinetic energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is oscillating with angular frequency of 176 rad/s. The frequency of this simple harmonic oscillator is ________ Hz. $\left[\text{take }\pi=\dfrac{22}{7}\right]$
questions.sol:
$K=\dfrac12m\omega^2A^2\cos^2\omega t=\dfrac14m\omega^2A^2(1+\cos2\omega t)$, so K varies at angular frequency $2\omega$.
$\omega=88$ rad/s and $f=\dfrac{88}{2\pi}=\dfrac{88\times7}{44}=14$ Hz.

questions.text: A capacitor $C$ is first charged fully with potential difference of $V_0$ and disconnected from the battery. The charged capacitor is connected across an inductor having inductance $L$. In $t$ s 25% of the initial energy in the capacitor is transferred to the inductor. The value of $t$ is _________s.
questions.sol:
$q=Q\cos\omega t$ with $\omega=\dfrac1{\sqrt{LC}}$, so the capacitor energy is $U_0\cos^2\omega t$.
25% transferred means $\cos^2\omega t=\dfrac34$, i.e. $\omega t=\dfrac\pi6$ (first time).
$t=\dfrac{\pi\sqrt{LC}}{6}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two known resistances of $R\ \Omega$ and $2R\ \Omega$ and one unknown resistance $X\ \Omega$ are connected in a circuit as shown in the figure. If the equivalent resistance between points $A$ and $B$ in the circuit is $X\ \Omega$, then the value of $X$ is __________ $\Omega$.
questions.sol:
$(2R+X)$ is in parallel with $R$: $\dfrac{R(2R+X)}{3R+X}=X$.
$2R^2+RX=3RX+X^2 \Rightarrow X^2+2RX-2R^2=0$.
$X=(\sqrt3-1)R$ (positive root).

questions.text: The total length of potentiometer wire AB is 50 cm in the arrangement as shown in figure. If $P$ is the point where the galvanometer shows zero reading then the length AP is __________ cm.
questions.sol:
With zero galvanometer current the arrangement is a balanced bridge: $\dfrac{AP}{PB}=\dfrac{6}{4}$.
$AP=\dfrac{6}{10}\times50=30$ cm.

questions.text: An infinitely long straight wire carrying current $I$ is bent in a planer shape as shown in the diagram. The radius of the circular part is $r$. The magnetic field at the centre $O$ of the circular loop is :
questions.sol:
The figure lies in the $y$-$z$ plane with $\hat i$ out of the page.
Straight wire (along $+\hat j$, a distance $r$ below O): $\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r}$ along $+\hat i$.
Circular loop: the current runs clockwise as seen from $+x$, so $\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2r}$ along $-\hat i$.
Net: $-\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r}(\pi-1)\hat i$.

questions.text:
Consider two identical metallic spheres of radius $R$ each having charge $Q$ and mass $m$. Their centers have an initial separation of $4R$. Both the spheres are given an initial speed of $u$ towards each other. The minimum value of $u$, so that they can just touch each other is :
(Take $k=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}$ and assume $kQ^2>Gm^2$ where $G$ is the Gravitational constant)
questions.sol:
Net interaction energy $U(d)=\dfrac{kQ^2-Gm^2}{d}$ (repulsive overall).
From $d=4R$ to touching ($d=2R$): $\Delta U=(kQ^2-Gm^2)\left(\dfrac1{2R}-\dfrac1{4R}\right)=\dfrac{kQ^2-Gm^2}{4R}$.
Initial KE $2\cdot\dfrac12mu^2=mu^2=\Delta U$, so $u=\sqrt{\dfrac{kQ^2}{4mR}\left(1-\dfrac{Gm^2}{kQ^2}\right)}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A battery with EMF $E$ and internal resistance $r$ is connected across a resistance $R$. The power consumption in $R$ will be maximum when :
questions.sol: $P=\dfrac{E^2R}{(R+r)^2}$. $\dfrac{dP}{dR}=0$ gives $(R+r)-2R=0$, i.e. $R=r$ (maximum power transfer).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : In a Young's double slit experiment, the angular separation of fringes will increase as the screen is moved away from the plane of the slits
Statement II : In a Young's double slit experiment, the angular separation of fringes will increase when monochromatic source is replaced by another monochromatic source of higher wavelength
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Angular fringe separation $=\dfrac{\lambda}{d}$, independent of the screen distance $D$, so Statement I is false.
It grows with $\lambda$, so Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
As shown in the diagram, when the incident ray is parallel to base of the prism, the emergent ray grazes along the second surface.
If refractive index of the material of prism is $\sqrt{2}$, the angle $\theta$ of prism is.
questions.sol:
The first face makes $45^\circ$ with the base, so a ray parallel to the base meets it at $i=45^\circ$: $\sin45^\circ=\sqrt2\sin r_1 \Rightarrow r_1=30^\circ$.
Grazing emergence means $r_2$ equals the critical angle: $\sin r_2=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$, $r_2=45^\circ$.
Apex angle $A=r_1+r_2=75^\circ$, so $\theta=180^\circ-45^\circ-75^\circ=60^\circ$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The energy of an electron in an orbit of the Bohr's atom is $-0.04E_0$ eV where $E_0$ is the ground state energy. If $L$ is the angular momentum of the electron in this orbit and $h$ is the Planck's constant, then $\dfrac{2\pi L}{h}$ is __________ :
questions.sol:
$E_n=\dfrac{E_1}{n^2}$; the energy is $0.04=\dfrac1{25}$ of the ground-state value, so $n=5$.
$L=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$ gives $\dfrac{2\pi L}{h}=n=5$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The charge stored by the capacitor C in the given circuit in the steady state is __________ $\mu$C.
questions.sol:
In the steady state no current flows in the capacitor branch. The diode with the 3 $\Omega$ resistor is reverse biased; the one with the 4 $\Omega$ resistor conducts.
Current $=\dfrac{2.5}{1+4}=0.5$ A, so the voltage across the parallel branches (and the capacitor, as its 2 $\Omega$ carries no current) is $0.5\times4=2$ V.
$Q=CV=5\times2=10\ \mu$C.

questions.text: The terminal velocity of a metallic ball of radius 6 mm in a viscous fluid is 20 cm/s. The terminal velocity of another ball of same material and having radius 3 mm in the same fluid will be __________ cm/s.
questions.sol:
Terminal velocity $\propto r^2$.
$v=20\times\left(\dfrac36\right)^2=5$ cm/s.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A diatomic gas $(\gamma=1.4)$ does 100 J of work when it is expanded isobarically. Then the heat given to the gas __________ J.
questions.sol:
Isobaric: $W=nR\Delta T$ and $Q=nC_p\Delta T$ with $C_p=\dfrac{\gamma R}{\gamma-1}=\dfrac72R$.
$Q=\dfrac72W=350$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
An electromagnetic wave of frequency 100 MHz propagates through a medium of conductivity, $\sigma=10$ mho/m. The ratio of maximum conduction current density to maximum displacement current density is __________.
$\left[\text{Take }\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_o}=9\times10^9\ \mathrm{Nm^2/C^2}\right]$
questions.sol:
Conduction current density $\sigma E_0$; displacement current density $\epsilon_0\omega E_0$ (taking the permittivity as $\epsilon_0$).
Ratio $=\dfrac{\sigma}{\omega\epsilon_0}=\dfrac{10\times4\pi\times9\times10^9}{2\pi\times10^8}=1800$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment set up, the two slits are kept 0.4. mm apart and screen is placed at 1 m from slits. If a thin transparent sheet of thickness 20 $\mu$m is introduced in front of one of the slits then center bright fringe shifts by 20 mm on the screen. The refractive index of transparent sheet is given by $\dfrac{\alpha}{10}$, where $\alpha$ is __________.

questions.text: A particle having electric charge $3\times10^{-19}$ C and mass $6\times10^{-27}$ kg is accelerated by applying an electric potential of 1.21 V. Wavelength of the matter wave associated with the particle is $\alpha\times10^{-12}$ m. The value of $\alpha$ is __________. (Take Planck's constant $=6.6\times10^{-34}$ J.s)
questions.sol:
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}=\dfrac{6.6\times10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2\times6\times10^{-27}\times3\times10^{-19}\times1.21}}$.
The square root is $\sqrt{43.56\times10^{-46}}=6.6\times10^{-23}$, so $\lambda=10^{-11}$ m $=10\times10^{-12}$ m.
$\alpha=10$.

questions.text: Aqueous HCl reacts with $\mathrm{MnO_2(s)}$ to form $\mathrm{MnCl_2(aq)}$, $\mathrm{Cl_2(g)}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O}(l)$. What is the weight (in g) of $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ liberated when 8.7 g of $\mathrm{MnO_2(s)}$ is reacted with excess aqueous HCl solution ? (Given Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ Mn $=55$, Cl $=35.5$, O $=16$, H $=1$)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{MnO_2+4HCl\rightarrow MnCl_2+Cl_2+2H_2O}$.
$\mathrm{MnO_2}$: $\dfrac{8.7}{87}=0.1$ mol, giving 0.1 mol $\mathrm{Cl_2}=7.1$ g.

questions.text:
Consider the following spectral lines for atomic hydrogen :
A. First line of Paschen series
B. Second line of Balmer series
C. Third line of Paschen series
D. Fourth line of Bracket series
The correct arrangement of the above lines in ascending order of energy is :
questions.sol:
Energy $\propto\dfrac1{n_1^2}-\dfrac1{n_2^2}$:
A ($4\to3$): $\dfrac19-\dfrac1{16}=0.0486$; B ($4\to2$): $\dfrac14-\dfrac1{16}=0.1875$; C ($6\to3$): $\dfrac19-\dfrac1{36}=0.0833$; D ($8\to4$): $\dfrac1{16}-\dfrac1{64}=0.0469$.
Ascending: D < A < C < B.

questions.text: The correct increasing order of C-H(A), C-O(B), C=O(C) and C$\equiv$N(D) bonds in terms of covalent bond length is :
questions.sol:
Typical bond lengths: C-H about 109 pm, C$\equiv$N about 116 pm, C=O about 121 pm, C-O about 143 pm.
Increasing order: A < D < C < B.

questions.text:
Consider the following data :
$\Delta_fH^\ominus$ (methane, g) $=-X$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
Enthalpy of sublimation of graphite $=Y$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
Dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{H_2}=Z$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
The bond enthalpy of C-H bond is given by :
questions.sol:
Atomisation of methane: $\mathrm{CH_4(g)\rightarrow C(g)+4H(g)}$, $\Delta H=4\varepsilon_{\mathrm{C-H}}$.
By Hess's law: $\Delta H=-\Delta_fH^\ominus(\mathrm{CH_4})+\Delta_{sub}H(\mathrm{C})+2\Delta_{diss}H(\mathrm{H_2})=X+Y+2Z$.
$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{C-H}}=\dfrac{X+Y+2Z}{4}$.

questions.text: For a closed circuit Daniell cell, which of the following plots is the accurate one at a given temperature ?
questions.sol:
$E^\circ_{cell}$ is the standard emf, fixed by the standard electrode potentials at a given temperature; it does not change as the cell runs (only $E_{cell}$ does).
So the plot of $E^\circ_{cell}$ against time is a horizontal line, option (4).

questions.text:
Decomposition of A is a first order reaction at T(K) and is given by $\mathrm{A(g)\longrightarrow B(g)+C(g)}$.
In a closed 1 L vessel, 1 bar A(g) is allowed to decompose at T(K). After 100 minutes, the total pressure was 1.5 bar. What is the rate constant (in min$^{-1}$) of the reaction ? ($\log2=0.3$)
questions.sol:
If $p$ bar of A reacts, total pressure $=1+p=1.5$, so $p=0.5$: half of A is gone in 100 min.
$t_{1/2}=100$ min, $k=\dfrac{2.303\log2}{100}=\dfrac{0.69}{100}=6.9\times10^{-3}$ min$^{-1}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The correct order in terms of atomic/ionic radii is $\mathrm{Al>Mg>Mg^{2+}>Al^{3+}}$.
Statement II : The correct order in terms of the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy is Cl>Br>S>O.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Mg (160 pm) is larger than Al (143 pm), so the order Al > Mg is wrong; Statement I is false.
Magnitudes of electron gain enthalpy: Cl (349) > Br (325) > S (200) > O (141 kJ mol$^{-1}$). Statement II is true.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The correct order in terms of bond dissociation enthalpy is $\mathrm{Cl_2>Br_2>F_2>I_2}$.
Statement II : The correct trend in the covalent character of the metal halides is $\mathrm{[SnCl_4>SnCl_2]}$, $\mathrm{[PbCl_4>PbCl_2]}$ and $\mathrm{[UF_4>UF_6]}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Bond dissociation enthalpies: $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ 242 > $\mathrm{Br_2}$ 192 > $\mathrm{F_2}$ 158 > $\mathrm{I_2}$ 151 kJ mol$^{-1}$ ($\mathrm{F_2}$ is low because of lone-pair repulsion). Statement I is true.
A higher oxidation state polarises the anion more, so covalent character increases with charge: $\mathrm{UF_6>UF_4}$, not the reverse. Statement II is false.

questions.text:
Given below are some of the statements about Mn and $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$. Identify the correct statements.
A. Mn forms the oxide $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$, in which Mn is in its highest oxidation state.
B. Oxygen stabilizes the Mn in higher oxidation states by forming multiple bonds with Mn.
C. $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$ is an ionic oxide.
D. The structure of $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$ consists of one bridged oxygen.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: Mn is +7 in $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$, its highest state: true.
B: oxygen stabilises high oxidation states through multiple bonding: true.
C: $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$ is a covalent (green oily) oxide: false.
D: its structure is two $\mathrm{MnO_4}$ tetrahedra sharing one oxygen: true.
Answer: A, B and D only.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) of $\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$ is greater than that of $\mathrm{[Mn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$.
Statement II : Potassium ferricyanide has a greater spin-only magnetic moment than sodium ferrocyanide.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ ($d^4$, high spin $t_{2g}^3e_g^1$): CFSE $=-0.6\Delta_o$; $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ ($d^5$, high spin): CFSE $=0$. Statement I is true.
$\mathrm{K_3[Fe(CN)_6]}$: low-spin $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ ($d^5$), 1 unpaired electron, 1.73 BM; $\mathrm{Na_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$: low-spin $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ ($d^6$), 0. Statement II is true.

By usual analysis, 1.00 g of compound (X) gave 1.79 g of magnesium pyrophosphate. The percentage of phosphorus in compound (X) is : (nearest integer)
(Given, molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ : O $=16$, Mg $=24$, P $=31$)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Mg_2P_2O_7}$: $M=48+62+112=222$, containing 62 g P.
%P $=\dfrac{62}{222}\times\dfrac{1.79}{1.00}\times100\approx50$.

questions.text:
The correct order of the rate of the reaction for the following reaction with respect to nucleophiles is :
$\mathrm{CH_3Br+Nu^\ominus\longrightarrow CH_3Nu+Br^\ominus}$
questions.sol:
This is an $S_N2$ reaction at a methyl carbon, so the rate follows nucleophilicity, which here parallels basicity (same attacking atom, O).
The more the negative charge is delocalised, the weaker the nucleophile: $\mathrm{OH^-}$ (localised) > $\mathrm{PhO^-}$ (ring delocalisation) > $\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}$ (over two O) > $\mathrm{ClO_4^-}$ (over four O).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Compound (X), shown below, dissolves in $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ solution and has two chiral carbon atoms
Statement II : Compound (Y), shown below, has two carbons with $sp^3$ hybridization, one carbon with $sp^2$ and one carbon with $sp$ hybridization
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
(X) has a COOH group, so it dissolves in $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ with effervescence; the two ring carbons carrying the aroyl and the COOH groups are both chiral. Statement I is true.
(Y) is $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH=C=O}$: $\mathrm{CH_3}$ and $\mathrm{CH_2}$ are $sp^3$, CH= is $sp^2$, and the central C of C=C=O is $sp$. Statement II is true.

questions.text: The correct order of reactivity of the following benzyl halides towards reaction with KCN is :
questions.sol:
The final key ranks them by how well the ring substituent stabilises a positive charge on the benzylic carbon.
$\mathrm{-NH_2}$ (b) is the strongest electron donor, then $\mathrm{-OH}$ (a). $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ withdraws electrons; at the meta position (d) it acts only inductively, while at the para position (c) it also withdraws by resonance, so c is the least reactive.
Order: b > a > d > c.

questions.text: Consider the above sequence of reactions. The number of bromine atom(s) in the final product (P) will be :
questions.sol:
(1) $\mathrm{NO_2}$ is meta-directing: 3-bromonitrobenzene. (2)-(3) Reduction gives 3-bromoaniline.
(4) Bromine water brominates every free position ortho/para to $\mathrm{NH_2}$ (2, 4, 6): 2,3,4,6-tetrabromoaniline.

questions.text:
The correct statements are :
A. Activation energy for enzyme catalysed hydrolysis of sucrose is lower than that of acid catalysed hydrolysis.
B. During denaturation, secondary and tertiary structures of a protein are destroyed but primary structure remains intact.
C. Nucleotides are joined together by glycosidic linkage between $\mathrm{C_1}$ and $\mathrm{C_4}$ carbons of the pentose sugar.
D. Quaternary structure of proteins represents overall folding of the polypeptide chain.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: enzymes lower the activation energy more than acids do: true.
B: denaturation leaves the peptide sequence intact: true.
C: nucleotides are linked by phosphodiester bonds (between C5$^\prime$ and C3$^\prime$): false.
D: overall folding of a chain is tertiary structure; quaternary structure is the arrangement of subunits: false.
Answer: A and B only.

questions.text: On heating a mixture of common salt and $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$ in equal amount along with concentrated $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ in a test tube, a gas is evolved. Formula of the gas evolved and oxidation state of the central metal atom in the gas respectively are :
questions.sol:
This is the chromyl chloride test: orange-red vapours of $\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}$ are evolved.
Oxidation state of Cr: $x+2(-2)+2(-1)=0 \Rightarrow x=+6$.

questions.text:
A substance 'X' (1.5 g) dissolved in 150 g of a solvent 'Y' (molar mass $=300$ g mol$^{-1}$) led to an elevation of the boiling point by 0.5 K. The relative lowering in the vapour pressure of the solvent 'Y' is __________ $\times10^{-2}$. (nearest integer)
[Given : $K_b$ of the solvent $=5.0$ K kg mol$^{-1}$]
Assume the solution to be dilute and no association or dissociation of X takes place in solution.
questions.sol:
Molality $=\dfrac{\Delta T_b}{K_b}=\dfrac{0.5}{5}=0.1$ mol kg$^{-1}$, so moles of X $=0.1\times0.150=0.015$.
Moles of Y $=\dfrac{150}{300}=0.5$.
Relative lowering $\approx\dfrac{n_X}{n_Y}=\dfrac{0.015}{0.5}=0.03=3\times10^{-2}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The osmotic pressure of a living cell is 12 atm at 300 K. The strength of sodium chloride solution that is isotonic with the living cell at this temperature is _________ g L$^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
Given : $R=0.08$ L atm K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$
Assume complete dissociation of NaCl
(Given : Molar mass of Na and Cl are 23 and 35.5 g mol$^{-1}$ respectively.)
questions.sol:
$\pi=iCRT$ with $i=2$: $12=2\times C\times0.08\times300 \Rightarrow C=0.25$ mol L$^{-1}$.
Strength $=0.25\times58.5\approx14.6$ g L$^{-1}$, i.e. 15.

questions.text: The first and second ionization constants of $\mathrm{H_2X}$ are $2.5\times10^{-8}$ and $1.0\times10^{-13}$ respectively. The concentration of $\mathrm{X^{2-}}$ in 0.1 M $\mathrm{H_2X}$ solution is __________ $\times10^{-15}$ M. (Nearest Integer)
questions.sol:
The first step gives $[\mathrm{H^+}]\approx[\mathrm{HX^-}]$; the second step is far weaker and hardly changes them.
$K_{a2}=\dfrac{[\mathrm{H^+}][\mathrm{X^{2-}}]}{[\mathrm{HX^-}]}\Rightarrow[\mathrm{X^{2-}}]\approx K_{a2}=1.0\times10^{-13}$ M $=100\times10^{-15}$ M.

questions.text:
MX is a sparingly soluble salt that follows the given solubility equilibrium at 298 K.
$\mathrm{MX(s)\rightleftharpoons M^+(aq)+X^-(aq)}$; $K_{sp}=10^{-10}$
If the standard reduction potential for $\mathrm{M^+(aq)\xrightarrow{+e^-}M(s)}$ is $\left(E^\ominus_{\mathrm{M^+/M}}\right)=0.79$ V, then the value of the standard reduction potential for the metal/metal insoluble salt electrode $E^\ominus_{\mathrm{X^-/MX(s)/M}}$ is _________ mV. (nearest integer)
$\left[\text{Given : }\dfrac{2.303RT}{F}=0.059\text{ V}\right]$
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{MX(s)+e^-\rightarrow M(s)+X^-}$ is $\mathrm{M^++e^-\rightarrow M}$ combined with $\mathrm{MX\rightarrow M^++X^-}$.
$E^\ominus_{\mathrm{X^-/MX/M}}=E^\ominus_{\mathrm{M^+/M}}+0.059\log K_{sp}=0.79+0.059(-10)=0.20$ V.
$=200$ mV.

questions.text: Identify the metal ions among $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{V^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$ having a spin-only magnetic moment value more than 3.0 BM. The sum of unpaired electrons present in the high spin octahedral complexes formed by those metal ions is __________.
questions.sol:
More than 3.0 BM needs at least 3 unpaired electrons (2 unpaired gives 2.83 BM).
High spin: $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$ $d^7$: 3; $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ $d^8$: 2; $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ $d^6$: 4; $\mathrm{V^{3+}}$ $d^2$: 2; $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$ $d^2$: 2.
Qualifying ions: $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$; sum $=3+4=7$.
